text:
Juuse Saros has been one of the best goalies in the league this season, and the Predators' climb has run straight through him. He has started all 13 games he has played, gone 6-3-4, and saved 9.2 goals more than the shots he faced usually produce (32 allowed on 41.2 expected), in the 85th percentile among goalies.

That is a sharp turn from last season, when our numbers had him 10.2 goals below expected in 59 games (Evolving-Hockey, on its own scale, was kinder). He has been at his best lately: 6.31 goals above expected over his last five starts, capped by a shutout in Los Angeles on Nov. 10, and only two goals allowed in the two games before it.

The detail that makes it credible is spread across the danger bands. He has been above league average on low (.982), medium (.876) and high-danger shots (.727 against a league .685). Thirteen starts is still a small sample for a goalie. The Athletic's Jesse Granger noted his new mask pays tribute to Dolly Parton. Nashville will take that look if the saves keep coming with it.
headline: Juuse Saros looks like Juuse Saros again
